campaign: Level-4 Priority 4 theory generalization beyond the closed Gaussian core
approach: generalize the closed P1/P2/P3 derivative and stability mechanism from the frozen Gaussian model to regular location families, and identify exactly which steps are Gaussian

lean.consumption_rationale: Priority 4 generalizes rather than restates: it imports the closed Priority-3 synthesis spine (which itself imports P1 and P2), proves the abstract-likelihood derivative bridge under a strictly weaker Lipschitz hypothesis, and derives the closed Gaussian statement from it as an instance.

conventions_inherited_unchanged.residual_convention: Z_t = eps_t - e, f_e(z) = f(z+e), parameter score s = f'/f = -psi (location_family / location_family_track3ab)
conventions_inherited_unchanged.window: w_m=min(m,tau), denominator w_m, terminal increment included (m_gt_1_priority1)

prior_art_within_repository.location_family: LOCATION-FAMILY-THEOREM-PARTIAL -- proved the stopped-score identity for a general regular location family, applied to the single terminal observation (m = 1) only
prior_art_within_repository.location_family_track3ab: LOCATION-FAMILY-TRACK3AB-CLOSED -- replicated that m = 1 result and compiled a conditional Lean spine in which the stopped-score derivative bridge is an assumed hypothesis
prior_art_within_repository.priority4_delta: m >= 1 truncated window with the random denominator and the tau < m branch; both frozen detectors in one statement; the weaker Lipschitz differentiation hypothesis (which admits Laplace and which the closed spines' dominated-derivative hypothesis excludes); the neutrality corollary; the sign analysis of the short-window correction; the proved moving-support and first-moment failure modes; a Lean proof of the bridge that Track 3A/3B assumed

evidence_boundary: Interval certification covers one closed-form unbounded-horizon Laplace instance, one exactly rational moving-support counterexample, and one finite-support general-score witness. Every frozen CUSUM and SR gain in this campaign, Gaussian or non-Gaussian, is a Monte Carlo estimate.
